summary: William Carlson Smith studied at Grand Island College (graduating by 1907), the University of Southern California, and the University of Chicago (~1912-1920). In Indology and other fields, he conducted educational work for the American Baptist Missionary Union (1912-1915).

Working in Indology, William Chambers served as a political servant for the East India Company (~1765-1793). He was an interpreter at the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (1775-1792) and a member of The Asiatic Society (~1784-1793).

William Charles Macready studied at Christ Church (~1850-1852) and the East India Company College (~1852-1854). Active in Indology, he served as an Assistant Government Agent in the Ceylon Civil Service in 1854.

Specializing in religious studies, philosophy, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, William Chittick studied at the University of Tehran (~1966-1974). He held posts at Sharif University of Technology, University at Albany, and Stony Brook University (~1983).

William Doderet studied at Balliol College, Oxford, earning his M.A. in 1880. Working in the fields of Indology and linguistics, he was University Teacher of Marathi at the University of Cambridge from 1910 to 1919.

William Douglas Penneck Hill studied as a scholar at King's College, Cambridge (~1903-1907). In Indology, he served as Assistant Master at Eton College (~1908-1913) and Principal at Jay Narayan Inter College (~1914-1928).

Whitney studied at Williams College, Berlin, and Tübingen under Salisbury, Weber, Roth, and Lepsius. A linguist and Indologist, he was Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Yale (1853, 1869-1894) and served as President of the American Oriental Society.

Working in philosophy and Buddhist studies, William Edelglass has held posts as a philosophy instructor at Colby College (attested 2007), professor at Marlboro College (attested 2013), and visiting professor at the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

William Edward Soothill studied at the University of London. Active in sinology and Buddhist studies, he served as Director at Shanxi University (1907-1911), worked at National Central University (1911), and was Professor of Chinese at Oxford (1920-1935).

William Erskine studied at the Royal High School and the University of Edinburgh (~1787-1792). Active in Indology, history, archaeology, and Iranian studies, he founded the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (1804) and served as Secretary and Vice-President (~1804-1823).
William Evans Hoyle studied at Owens College (~1872-1874) and Christ Church, Oxford (~1874-1877).

William F. Powell works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. He held academic posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara, attested in 1986 and as Emeritus Professor of Religious Studies and Research Professor in 2026.

William Fairfield Warren studied at Wesleyan, Mystical Seven, and Andover Theological Seminary. Active in religious studies and philosophy, he taught at the Methodist Episcopal Missionary Institute (1860-1866) and was Boston University's first president and comparative theology professor (1873-1911).

Educated at the University of London (B.A.), William Foster worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held several posts at the India Office from 1882 to 1927, including Registrar and Superintendent of Records, and later served as President of the Hakluyt Society.

William Foxwell Albright studied at Upper Iowa University (~1907-1912) and Johns Hopkins University (~1913-1916). He was Acting Director at the American Schools of Oriental Research (1921-1922) and W. W. Spence Professor of Semitic Languages at Johns Hopkins (1929-1958).
Active in history, archaeology, and Indology, William Francklin received his education at Westminster School (~1777-1781) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1781-1782).

William Frederic Sinclair was educated at the Royal School, Armagh. Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, he joined the Indian Civil Service in 1866 and held administrative positions in the Bombay Presidency from approximately 1869 to 1893.

Working in Tibetology, William Frederick Travers O'Connor studied at Charterhouse School (1884-1887) and the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (~1888-1890). He received a post in the Royal Artillery in 1890.
William Frederick Webster studied at the City of London School, at Trinity College, Cambridge (1874) under Edward Byles Cowell, and at Lincoln's Inn (1879). His field was Indology.

William G. Archer studied at the University of Cambridge (~1926-1930) and SOAS University of London (~1930-1931). In the fields of Indology, history, and archaeology, he was Keeper of the Indian Section at the Victoria and Albert Museum (1949-1959).
